run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T16:24:56Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is a downstream symptom of product-catalog becoming unavailable. At 16:25:08-16:25:24 the product-catalog Deployment rolled out a new ReplicaSet (product-catalog-56fbb5f966) whose pod template image is quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0; every pull attempt fails with 401 UNAUTHORIZED, the old working ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog) was scaled 1→0, and its pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-qz548 was deleted. The only product-catalog pod is now Pending in ImagePullBackOff, the product-catalog Service (100.69.9.250:8080) has only a not-ready endpoint, and product-catalog span volume fell from ~3500/5m to 0. Frontend calls to ProductCatalogService fail with gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE (connect EPERM 100.69.9.250:8080) and recommendation's ListProducts likewise; frontend then returns HTTP 500 on /api/products/{productId}, /api/recommendations and /api/checkout, which frontend-proxy logs and spans record as 500 'via_upstream' responses from the frontend cluster. frontend-proxy itself is fully ready (1/1) with 0 restarts, so the alert reflects upstream failures passing through it. Recommendation and checkout errors are the same failed ProductCatalogService calls; cart and /api/data traffic still shows 200s.

claims.text: frontend-proxy span errors are essentially new after 16:25: over the 75m to 16:40:09, increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}) is 9134.83, split as span_name "ingress" 4573.52 and "router frontend egress" 4561.31, while its total UNSET-status spans are 39395.72. Baseline per-5m error increases were 1.25, 1.11, 3.33, 2.5 before 16:24:56 and then 3834.44 (window ending 16:29:56), 3898.75 and 2324.26.

frontend-proxy's own container log for 16:26:00-16:40:00 contains 6014 matching lines; the newest 20 (16:34:36.265Z-16:34:37.749Z) are HTTP 500 responses on "GET /api/products/<id>", "POST /api/checkout" and "GET /api/data/" with "via_upstream" and upstream cluster "frontend" (e.g. "POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream ... frontend), while "POST /api/cart" and "GET /api/data" return 200.

frontend error spans jump from 0 in the windows up to 16:24:56 to 6937.15, 7850 and 4556.03 per 5m afterwards; broken down by operation, errors are on GET /api/products/{productId} (1273.28, 2593.44, 2350.66), executing api route /api/products/[productId], grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, GET /api/recommendations (218.12, 483.54, 471.25), POST /api/checkout (163.16, 325.56, 279.18) and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, with zero errors on cart routes.

Sampled error traces show the chain load-generator GET(error,500) -> frontend-proxy "ingress"(error,500) -> frontend-proxy "router frontend egress"(error,500) -> frontend GET(error,500) -> frontend "executing api route (pages) /api/products/[productId]" -> frontend "grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct" with otel.status_code=ERROR and rpc.grpc.status_code=14, error message "14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect EPERM 100.69.9.250:8080".

recommendation spans fail calling product-catalog: "get_product_list" raises grpc._channel._InactiveRpcError and its child "/oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts" has rpc.grpc.status_code=14 with details "failed to connect to all addresses; last error: UNKNOWN: ipv4:100.69.9.250:8080: connect: Operation not permitted (1)"; the parent frontend "grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations" span then reports rpc.grpc.status_code=2 and HTTP 500 on "GET /api/recommendations".

The failing address 100.69.9.250:8080 is the otel-demo Service "product-catalog" (ClusterIP 100.69.9.250, port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=product-catalog), and its Endpoints object currently holds only notReadyAddresses pointing at pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk (ip 100.96.4.116) with no ready addresses.

Deployment product-catalog (otel-demo) has 1 desired replica, updatedReplicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1 and Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable; its pod template image is quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0.

Ownership chain: ReplicaSet product-catalog-56fbb5f966 (created 2026-11-16T16:25:08Z, replicas 1, no ready/available replicas) is owned by Deployment product-catalog and uses image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0, while the previous ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc (created 15:51:35Z, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog) is scaled to replicas 0.

Pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk (owner ReplicaSet product-catalog-56fbb5f966) is Pending and not Ready, container "product-catalog" waiting with reason ImagePullBackOff and message: Back-off pulling image "quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0": ErrImagePull: failed to pull and unpack image: failed to resolve image: unexpected status from HEAD request to https://quay.io/v2/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid/manifests/1.0.0: 401 UNAUTHORIZED.

Events in otel-demo record the rollout: 16:25:09 pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-8rw7j created/Scheduled, 16:25:12 Failed to pull image (401 UNAUTHORIZED)+ErrImagePull, 16:25:13 BackOff/ImagePullBackOff, 16:25:16 old pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-qz548 "Stopping container"/deleted and ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc scaled down 1 to 0, 16:25:24 new pod product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk created, and further Failed/BackOff image-pull warnings at 16:28:34 and 16:30:39.

product-catalog span volume collapses with the rollout: 3508.75 spans in the 5m ending 16:24:56, 523.33 in the window ending 16:29:56, then 0 in the windows ending 16:34:56 and 16:39:56, i.e. the service stopped serving traffic.

checkout's errors are confined to its product-catalog call: increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}) over 15m is 155.59, 308.70 and 414 on span_name "oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct" and the identical values on "oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder", starting in the window ending 16:29:56.

At 16:39:56 the 5m error-span ratio for frontend-proxy's "ingress" operation is 0.5564 (55.6% of its ingress spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR); this is a span-level ratio for one operation, not the 18.19 value quoted in the alert annotation.

frontend-proxy's own workload is healthy: Deployment frontend-proxy has ready=1/available=1 with no unavailableReplicas on image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend-proxy, Deployment frontend likewise 1/1 ready, and pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-zj87n has restartCount 0 — so the errors are not caused by a restarting or unready proxy.

cart was checked and shows no failure evidence: no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series was returned for service_name="cart" in the 75m window (only STATUS_CODE_UNSET), the sampled trace's cart spans (POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, HGET, HMSET, EXPIRE) carry rpc.grpc.status_code=0, and frontend-proxy logs show "POST /api/cart" 200 and "GET /api/data" 200.

Rejected: a fault originating inside frontend-proxy (its own crash, resource exhaustion or proxy misconfiguration) as the cause of the alert. Its pod is Running with 0 restarts and its Deployment is fully available, and its error spans/logs are 500 responses received from the upstream "frontend" cluster (via_upstream) whose own error spans are failed ProductCatalogService gRPC calls.

Candidate, weakly supported: the gRPC client error text "connect: Operation not permitted (1)"/"connect EPERM 100.69.9.250:8080" could also be produced by a network-level connection rejection independent of the missing backend. Nothing observed supports it as the origin: the same address is the product-catalog ClusterIP whose only endpoint is the not-ready ImagePullBackOff pod, and the outage timeline starts exactly with that pod's rollout. No NetworkPolicy objects were returned for otel-demo, but that query returned no_data, so a network policy cannot be positively ruled out from it.

Roll the product-catalog Deployment back to the previously running image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog (or correct the image reference/registry credentials for quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0), then confirm a Ready product-catalog pod and a ready endpoint on Service product-catalog:8080 so frontend ProductCatalogService calls stop returning gRPC 14.

gaps: No alerting rule named RequestErrorRate was returned by Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned status no_data, citable_as_fact=false), so the exact alert expression and the 18.18888888888889 value in the annotation could not be verified; the span-level ratio measured here (0.5564) is not that metric.

Frontend container logs could not be read (fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-gx54w returned no_data for both the 16:25-16:40 error-filtered read and an unfiltered read), so frontend's application-log error text is unknown; the frontend failure attribution rests on its spans.
The old product-catalog pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-qz548 was deleted at 16:25:16, so its logs and termination details are unavailable; only its SuccessfulDelete/Killing events are known.
The pod that never started (product-catalog-56fbb5f966-h9xjk) has no container log lines (fetch_pod_logs returned no_data), consistent with the container never being created.
The NetworkPolicy check for otel-demo returned status no_data with zero objects, so a network-level cause cannot be positively excluded from that view.

Alert start 16:24:56Z precedes the first Failed image-pull event at 16:25:12Z by ~16s and the first new pod creation at 16:25:09Z; the precise trigger instant and alert evaluation window are unresolved.
No change-history integration is available, so who/what changed the product-catalog Deployment image is unknown.
next_steps: Restore product-catalog by reverting the Deployment image to ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog and verify pods become Ready with endpoints populated.

Inspect how quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-invalid:1.0.0 entered the Deployment manifest (source of change is outside the available data sources) and add admission/validation that rejects unpullable image references.
Review the RequestErrorRate alert rule definition and the metric behind the 18.18888888888889 reading, since the rule was not returned by this Prometheus.
Watch frontend-proxy, frontend, recommendation and checkout error rates to confirm they recover once product-catalog serves traffic again.
